question_variants: how many customers are we losing
sql:
WITH monthly_active AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.user_id, FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', oi.created_at) AS month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
  WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
),
month_pairs AS (
  SELECT m1.month AS current_month,
    MIN(m2.month) AS next_month
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT month FROM monthly_active) m1
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT month FROM monthly_active) m2 ON m2.month > m1.month
  GROUP BY m1.month
)
SELECT mp.current_month AS month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS active_users,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.user_id IS NULL THEN a.user_id END) AS churned,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.user_id IS NULL THEN a.user_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id), 0), 2) AS churn_rate_pct
FROM month_pairs mp
JOIN monthly_active a ON a.month = mp.current_month
LEFT JOIN monthly_active b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.month = mp.next_month
GROUP BY mp.current_month
ORDER BY mp.current_month
report: Churn rate is the percentage of active users in month M who placed no orders in month M+1. A user who returns in M+2 still counts as churned in M. Always distinguish churn from low activity — a user who buys less is not churned until they stop entirely.
